title: The early afterglow of GRB 190829A
question: Characterize the early stages of the multi-wavelength afterglow evolution of GRB 190829A and determine its emission mechanism, physics of the ejecta, and properties of the external medium.

what.value: Optical and near-IR follow-up measurements from GROND, UKIRT, TNG, NOT, MMT, and Liverpool Telescope reported via GCN notices

evidence.quote: We present in Figure 2 the IR measurements obtained by by GROND (cite: 2019GCN.25569....1C), UKIRT (cite: 2019GCN.25584....1P) and TNG (cite: 2019GCN.25591....1D) together with the optical fluxes measured by NOT (cite: 2019GCN.25563....1H), MMT (cite: 2019GCN.25583....1F) and the Liverpool Telescope (cite: 2019GCN.25585....1P; 2019GCN.25592....1B).

external_data.citation: GROND (cite: 2019GCN.25569....1C), UKIRT (cite: 2019GCN.25584....1P), TNG (cite: 2019GCN.25591....1D), NOT (cite: 2019GCN.25563....1H), MMT (cite: 2019GCN.25583....1F), Liverpool Telescope (cite: 2019GCN.25585....1P; 2019GCN.25592....1B)

what.value: Galactic hydrogen column density N_H = 5.6 x 10^20 cm^-2

evidence.quote: in addition to the Galactic value $N_H=5.6\times 10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$ (cite: Willingale2013).

what.value: Ratio log(E_K/n) ~ 54 used to infer circumburst density

evidence.quote: and the ratio log $(E_K/n) \approx$ 54 from (cite: Salafia2021), we infer a circumburst density $n\approx$0.01 - 0.1 cm$^{-3}$

what.value: Fermi/GBM observed peak energy E_peak^obs = 130 +/- 20 keV for the first pulse

evidence.quote: This value is consistent with the location of the peak energy close to the energy bandpass ($E_{peak}^{obs}$=$130 \pm 20$ keV), as derived from the Fermi/GBM analysis (cite: 2019GCN.25575....1L; Chand20).

recipe.goal: Measure ALMA millimeter/submillimeter flux densities and uncertainties
recipe.method: Retrieve final calibrated images from the ALMA archive, perform Gaussian fits and RMS image noise measurements in identical regions using CASA VIEWER(), and sum RMS and flux calibration uncertainties in quadrature.
key_parameters: Calibration uncertainty = 5% (Band 3), 10% (Band 7); upper limits at 3 sigma

recipe.goal: Reduce and image ATCA radio observations and extract flux densities
recipe.method: Process public ATCA datasets in Miriad via splitting, manual or sumthreshold flagging (pgflag), calibration, clean & restore imaging, and phase decorrelation correction (calred).
key_parameters: robust = 0 (6C configuration until 2019 Sep 13, all antennas); robust = 2 (H168 configuration past 2019 Sep 13, antenna-6 excluded); multiplicative systematic error = 3% (2.1-9.5 GHz), 5% (16.7-21.2 GHz)

recipe.goal: Reduce Swift BAT, XRT, and UVOT data and MASTER optical polarimetry
recipe.method: Process BAT light curves and spectra with HEASOFT and XSPEC, retrieve and convert XRT light curves, perform host-subtracted aperture photometry on UVOT images with HEADAS/UVOTSOURCE, and perform aperture photometry and Stokes Q calculation on MASTER polarized images.
key_parameters: UVOT extraction radius = 3'' aperture corrected to 5''; MASTER aperture size = 3.9''
assumptions: Galactic N_H = 5.6 x 10^20 cm^-2; afterglow and supernova negligible after 58 days in UVOT

recipe.goal: Model multi-wavelength light curves and broadband SEDs with Forward Shock and Reverse Shock components
recipe.method: Fit X-ray, UVOIR, and radio light curves with power laws and smoothly broken power laws; model broadband SEDs at 4 epochs (1200 s, 6800 s, 21600 s, 1 d) using two smoothly broken power-law components (FS and RS); test standard FS model using afterglowpy.
key_parameters: SED epochs: 1200 s, 6800 s, 21600 s, 1 d; FS spectral indices fixed to beta_low = -1/3 and beta_up = 0.75 (p ~ 2.50)
assumptions: Constant density external medium; standard fireball closure relations for FS

recipe.goal: Derive burst energetics, circumburst density, and jet opening angle
recipe.method: Calculate isotropic-equivalent kinetic energy from X-ray luminosity at 14 d, infer circumburst density using log(E_K/n) from literature, and derive lower limits on jet opening angle and collimation-corrected energy from the non-detection of a jet break up to 100 d.
key_parameters: t_j >= 100 d, nu_X ~ 5 keV at 14 d
assumptions: p = 2.5, fraction of emitting electrons xi = 1, epsilon_e = 0.1, epsilon_B = 10^-4, standard LambdaCDM cosmology

answer_key.quantity: Forward shock electron spectral index p

evidence.loc: A forward shock plus reverse shock scenario
evidence.quote: Using the standard closure relations for GRB afterglows, the post peak temporal slope, $\alpha \approx$1.1, is related to the spectral index of the accelerated electrons as $p$ = 4$\alpha$/3 +1 = 2.50 $\pm$0.16.

answer_key.quantity: Reverse shock electron spectral index p

evidence.quote: The second spectral component tracks the reverse shock (RS) modeled with spectral slopes of $\beta^{RS}_{low}$ $\approx$ -1.0 $\pm$0.2 and $\beta^{RS}_{up}$ $\approx$ 0.90$\pm$0.02, leading to $p$=2.80$\pm$0.04.

score_reason: ALMA analysis uses standard archival calibrated images with straightforward Gaussian fitting in CASA 5.4, and all extracted flux densities are tabulated in Table 4; minor ambiguity in exact fitting regions and custom SED fitting routines.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA archival calibrated images exist for both project codes, the measurement recipe (CASA Gaussian fitting + quadrature calibration uncertainty) is simple and well-specified, and all resulting flux densities and light-curve break parameters are explicitly tabulated.
